searchText: We have decided to do LIFO refund mechanism, in this particular case, the overcharged state gas will be repayed to regular first if the state_gas_spilled counter is non-zero. It should automatically address the concerns raised by <@1252939266871263294> right? Outcome would be same as what Luis proposed (i think), but yeah this is change for devnet-7 Isn't the LIFO already in glamsterdam-devnet-6? (I hate LIFO name) yeah it is for frames, but it didn't get included for eip7702 state refund, that gas is added back to reservoir always. ~~Yeah, I feel that we should use the LIFO for this case as well - if the charges were taken from reservoir, then give back to reservoir; if not, give back to gas_left~~ Edit: actually, <@1252939266871263294> proposal is cleaner, I think. So I feel we should go with that Outcome should be same, but Luis PR simplifies EIP text. Wait, I remember something: we don't want the intrinsic costs to depend on the state. So, we cannot change that during the auth processing so, we need to use LIFO True, we still want to check for max intrinsic gas, and then reduce intrinsic gas for amount of already existing accounts (and other checks). My small point here is that it should not matter that it is state refund, you can just decrease intrinsic gas and and then calculate reservoir from it. how can we decrease intrinsic gas without making a dependency between intrinsic costs and state? > We have decided to do LIFO refund mechanism, in this particular case, the overcharged state gas will be repayed to regular first if the state_gas_spilled counter is non-zero. It should automatically address the concerns raised by @lu-pinto right? 1. Being pragmatic about it, if one thinks this does not change consensus then why not going with this version which makes the EIP text much clearer? 2. AFAIK EIP text in this section is still wrong. It does not mention source based refunds anywhere and explicity says "refill the state reservoir..." 3. ACCOUNT_WRITE is refunded to `refund_counter` while this is just an overcharge correction. Why are we overcharging regular gas for compute that we are only giving back at the end? > how can we decrease intrinsic gas without making a dependency between intrinsic costs and state? <@968526635735326741> I remember you said this during ACDT but I personally did not understand, can you explain this angle a little more? Why creating a dependency between intrinsic costs and state is bad? If it's for mempool validation, then one should use max costs (intrinsic regular + state) all the time. Yes, I am mostly worried about mempool/focil validation and block inclusion validation before we start execution yeah but the validation step that gets triggered is the max charge so there's no depencency there ok, got it. Then I think your proposal makes sense > AFAIK EIP text in this section is still wrong. It does not mention source based refunds anywhere and explicity says "refill the state reservoir..." Yes it's true, we update the 7702 processing before the LIFO mechanism, the EIP is a bit inaccurate there. Thanks for pointing it out But isn;t that the whole point of IntrinsicCost? We need a static validation mechanism that allows the mempool to reject transactions earlier if they can never be accepted. Such validation should not depend on state, otherwise the outcome may differ between nodes or over time. Block processing should follow the same rule, treating mempool validation as a precondition and enforcing the same checks consistently. I think one thing I disagree is: we can't use the one rule in mempool validation while another rule in block processing. If we need to enforce this property with a consistent precondition, then the validation must be stateless. I was thinking further I actually think there could be a consensus difference between right now and returning funds to intrinsic costs during tx processing. So picture the following case: - You start with an empty reservoir because user provided `gas_limit <= MAX_TX_GAS_LIMIT`. You pay the max charges for the authorization list in `intrinsic_gas` and then put them back into `gasLeft` which is where you took them from initially, as per the source based refund mechanism. - Then you get a halt at the top frame so you loose all remaining gas - > you lost all the funds, even those overcharged for the EIP-7702 authorization processing. Might be missing something but if that's the case I don't think this is fair UX > I think one thing I disagree is: we can't use the one rule in mempool validation while another rule in block processing how is that the case with what I'm proposing? I'm saying do the same validation step in both cases but give funds back after to where you charged them -> `intrinsic_cost` Why? The fund losing is caused by the exceptional halt, it's consistent for all scenarios (except for non-empty reservoir) but you were overcharged initially though yeah I guess you loose all funds anyway, never mind we can use another scenario for comparison, we halt for some reasons and there are still non-zero `gasLeft`, we burn them anyway > but give funds back after to where you charged them -> intrinsic_cost Yes, but how will you implement that: intrinsic_cost represents a cost, we charge it beforehand, then we process the auths and need to refund the cost to somewhere intrinsic_cost is an immutable variable, we need to repay the cost to somewhere, we can't decrease the intrinsic_cost afterwards well you are thinking conceptually, it doesn't mean it's immutable at the implementation level 😄 But I guess if there's no difference from a consensus POV, these are all implementation details. I'm fine with that but what about the `refund_counter` part for `ACCOUNT_WRITE` ? That looks wrong though? My argument is: > The `(STATE_BYTES_PER_NEW_ACCOUNT + STATE_BYTES_PER_AUTH_BASE) × CPSB` portion is credited back to `intrinsic_state_gas` and the `ACCOUNT_WRITE` portion is credited back to `intrinsic_regular_gas`. I don't know how to implement it. The only way I will do is returning the cost back to it's original source, like what we did now. Honestly this text is confusing for me. I think we are using the legacy refund rule for regular cost. `ACCOUNT_WRITE` represents a database write, in term of regular dimension. If we refund that, we just put it in the refund counter yeah but my point is that no database write happened and you are being charged for it I agree. I guess your concern is we over-charge `ACCOUNT_WRITE` and the ultimate refunded amount is only 20% at most, this asymmetry makes you unhappy But we do the same thing for SSTORE. For example, we do 0->x->0, for `0->x`, we charge 20000; for `x->0`, we charge 100, refund 19900; the effective cost of the combo is 200. but unfortunately, the 19900 won't be fully returned even the database write doesn't happen yes it's the same if clients are optimized to not write during transaction execution but protocol does not see it that way? also that case is spread throughout execution, whereas the case we are discussing is localized even before execution starts

excerpts.author: lu_pinto
excerpts.content:
> We have decided to do LIFO refund mechanism, in this particular case, the overcharged state gas will be repayed to regular first if the state_gas_spilled counter is non-zero. It should automatically address the concerns raised by @lu-pinto right?

1. Being pragmatic about it, if one thinks this does not change consensus then why not going with this version which makes the EIP text much clearer?
2. AFAIK EIP text in this section is still wrong. It does not mention source based refunds anywhere and explicity says "refill the state reservoir..."
3. ACCOUNT_WRITE is refunded to `refund_counter` while this is just an overcharge correction. Why are we overcharging regular gas for compute that we are only giving back at the end?

excerpts.content:
> how can we decrease intrinsic gas without making a dependency between intrinsic costs and state?
<@968526635735326741> I remember you said this during ACDT but I personally did not understand, can you explain this angle a little more? Why creating a dependency between intrinsic costs and state is bad? If it's for mempool validation, then one should use max costs (intrinsic regular + state) all the time.

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content:
> AFAIK EIP text in this section is still wrong. It does not mention source based refunds anywhere and explicity says "refill the state reservoir..."
Yes it's true, we update the 7702 processing before the LIFO mechanism, the EIP is a bit inaccurate there. Thanks for pointing it out

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content:
But isn;t that the whole point of IntrinsicCost?

We need a static validation mechanism that allows the mempool to reject transactions earlier if they can never be accepted. Such validation should not depend on state, otherwise the outcome may differ between nodes or over time.

Block processing should follow the same rule, treating mempool validation as a precondition and enforcing the same checks consistently.

excerpts.author: garyrong
excerpts.content: I think one thing I disagree is: we can't use the one rule in mempool validation while another rule in block processing. If we need to enforce this property with a consistent precondition, then the validation must be stateless.

excerpts.author: lu_pinto
excerpts.content:
I was thinking further I actually think there could be a consensus difference between right now and returning funds to intrinsic costs during tx processing. So picture the following case:
- You start with an empty reservoir because user provided `gas_limit <= MAX_TX_GAS_LIMIT`. You pay the max charges for the authorization list in `intrinsic_gas` and then put them back into `gasLeft` which is where you took them from initially, as per the source based refund mechanism.
- Then you get a halt at the top frame so you loose all remaining gas - > you lost all the funds, even those overcharged for the EIP-7702 authorization processing.

Might be missing something but if that's the case I don't think this is fair UX
